items.followUp: Differentiate between frictional braking and skidding.

rubric.why: Identifies braking as using friction to reduce a vehicle’s speed.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that applying brakes uses friction to slow or stop the vehicle.

rubric.why: Distinguishes skidding as sliding rather than controlled rolling.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the wheels slide on the road, often causing loss of control.

modelAnswer: Braking is the use of brakes to reduce or stop a vehicle’s motion by friction.
Skidding occurs when the wheels slide over the road instead of rolling normally, and the driver may lose control.

items.followUp: State Newton’s second law of motion and give one example.

rubric.why: States the equal-and-opposite relationship between action and reaction forces.
rubric.how: Award for stating that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of action and reaction.
rubric.how: Award for a suitable example, such as gun recoil, walking, or swimming.

modelAnswer: Newton’s third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Example: When a gun is fired, the bullet moves forward and the gun recoils backward.

items.followUp: Define the point of application of a force.

rubric.why: Defines the line of action as the line along which the force acts.
rubric.how: Award both marks for identifying it as the straight line along which the force acts; award one mark for identifying it as the force’s line or direction.

modelAnswer: The line of action of a force is the straight line along which the force acts.

items.followUp: Define density and write its formula and SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines pressure as force acting per unit area.
rubric.how: Award for stating force per unit area.
Award for the formula P = F/A and the SI unit pascal (Pa), equivalent to N/m².

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting per unit area of a surface.
Formula: P = F/A.
SI unit: pascal (Pa), which is equal to N/m².

items.followUp: Define stress and state whether it has a unit.

rubric.why: Identifies strain as a ratio of a change in dimension to the original dimension.
rubric.how: Award for stating the ratio of change in length (or dimension) to original length (or dimension).

rubric.why: Recognises that a ratio of like quantities has no unit.
rubric.how: Award for stating that strain has no unit or is dimensionless.

modelAnswer: Strain is the ratio of the change in length of a body to its original length.
Strain has no unit; it is dimensionless.

items.followUp: What is a thermometer? Name the two common types used in a laboratory and for measuring body temperature.

rubric.how: Award for defining a thermometer as an instrument used to measure temperature.

rubric.why: Names the two commonly taught types.
rubric.how: Award for naming clinical and laboratory thermometers.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
Its two types are the clinical thermometer and the laboratory thermometer.

items.followUp: Define rest and explain translatory, rotatory, and vibratory motion.

rubric.why: Defines motion by a change in position with time relative to surroundings.
rubric.how: Award for stating that motion is a change in position with time relative to surroundings.

rubric.why: Describes translatory motion as the motion of a body from one place to another, with its parts moving together.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming and describing translatory motion.
Award for stating that a body rotates about an axis.

rubric.why: Identifies repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a body moves to and fro about a mean position.

modelAnswer: Motion is the change in position of a body with respect to its surroundings as time passes.
Translatory motion: A body moves from one place to another; all parts of the body move together.
Rotatory motion: A body turns about a fixed axis.
Vibratory motion: A body moves to and fro about its mean position.

items.followUp: How much time is required for a force of 15 N to change momentum by 30 N·s?

rubric.why: Correctly records the given change in momentum and force in SI units.
rubric.how: Award for identifying Δp = 22 N·s and F = 20 N.

rubric.why: Uses the impulse-momentum relationship to find time.
rubric.how: Award for a correct formula, such as Δp = Ft or t = Δp/F.
Award for substituting 22 N·s and 20 N into t = Δp/F.

rubric.why: Gives the correctly calculated time with its unit.
rubric.how: Award both marks for 1.1 s; award one mark for the correct numerical value without a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Change in momentum, Δp = 22 N·s; force, F = 20 N.
Formula: Δp = Ft, so t = Δp/F.
Substitution: t = (22 N·s)/(20 N).
Answer: t = 1.1 s.
